items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: It was also the first time for Ray to play in Europe and the first time I ever heard him and saw him.

ctx.x: were some jazz lovers there too and we had our success also, but quieter.....

Juan-les-Pins had become very well known for its annual jazz festival. It was the second year that the festival was presented and the orchestras of Ray Charles and Count Basie were the big attractions. It was also the first time for Ray to play in Europe and the first time I ever heard him and saw him. He had a small group with two trumpets, three sax, bass and drums and the Raylettes. He sent me with his style of playing and singing and the arrangements were swinging like mad.

As I was already in Juan-le -Pins, one of the organisers, of the festival, a Monsieur Souplet whom I had known for a long time, wanted me to play one evening at the festival. He told me that there was going to be a very good trio playing that week and he thought that it would be an ideal group to accompany me. It was the trio of the pianist Les McCann.
